title: Borderlands: The Pre-Sequel
text: Borderlands: The Pre-Sequel is Borderlands in space and the best Borderlands so far. The first Borderlands introduced us a lovely shoot 'n' loot game with a rich world full of tales and wicked characters. One of the most tiring things while also being part of its charm was actually the part of Pandora that we saw. The surroundings. Sand, sand and more sand combined with fifty shades of brown. Me and my co-op partner felt like drowning in sand and dust after the playthrough. After all this Borderlands 2 rose like a phoenix and showed us Pandora in a completely different light with green pastures and maps that weren't only taken from Mad Max! With a story that for the first time felt like a proper story and more lunatic fellows and guns and loot and more everything, it made the first part look shameful. Most of the aspects from the old parts are here in The Pre-Sequel, just better or at least at the same level of quality. In the story we see our beloved villain Handsome Jack's path from a wannabe hero into the horrible monster of Borderlands 2. The gameplay is the same old good Borderlands that you have gotten used to with some space twists like weaker gravity and the often absence of areas with oxygen. Jumping in space is seriously fun and also convenient, so it's pretty hard to get used to gravity again. Anyway, I'd like to praise the story. Who crazy plays Borderlands for their stories? I do, especially from now on. The jokes are as funny as ever if you find the Borderlands humor endearing and the plot is interesting to follow while exploding heads just like in the second part. The feature that I experienced as compelling was the fact that your Vault Hunters finally join the discussions and are more engaged in the story instead of just some random catchlines. This adds a good amount of replay value for those who are not only interested in different skill trees but also in interacting characters. I felt like really being part of the story and not just a mute shell doing quests. Something that seems so minor was a huge change in my eyes. Why wasn't it always done like this? It's a good start and even more dialogue from the Vault Hunters is what I absolutely desire. Remember the complaining about dust? I love space. There's a lot of space in this game. The areas aren't boring though and shouldn't make you want to never see space again, but at the same time the game maps aren't from as large scale as in Borderlands 2. For a guy like me who sees dreams of Mass Effect, I can't say I mind too much. The Pre-Sequel doesn't reinvent the wheel, it attaches rockets to the wheel and sends it out of Pandora. And the wheel speaks now. That's enough for me, but for the next game it's only reasonable to demand bigger differences. The series is going into a great direction and I expect wonderful things from Borderlands 3. Meanwhile, enjoy the fresh air of Elpis!

title: Boson X
text: 10.7h  (based on steam). No. No. Yes (5 achievements; can be more or less based on your skill). No (last response is in 25 Apr 2016). Boson X is a quick fast paced runner game where you have to dodge obstacles and step on blue colored platform to collect some sort of percentage. The game will finish after you earn 100%, although you can still continue after that to aim for high score in an altered colored mode. There is also a high score list which is sorted by the said percentage. This game is using 2D models on 3D environment and the characters are soft colored. I really like the character design and animation when they are running through the stages. The UI is also simple and easy to understand. There are roughly 6 bgms in total which is played in each area. Each bgm has their own different characteristic and I really like the music except for the Graviton and Dark X Boson stage. The first one sounds like you're in temple and the second one is way too quiet. This game is easy to learn but hard to master. You just have to jump through obstacles and (or) move left and right to dodge them. At some point, there will be a blue platform which will help you obtain some percentage. You'll finish the stage after you obtain 100%, although you still can continue the game to aim for high score in an altered color afterwards which might hurt your eyes. The more percentage you have, the faster your character will run. There are 3 different areas which consists of 6 stages. Each area has its own unique mechanics which is slightly different from each other. The first few stages will serve as a tutorial (yet still difficult for beginners) to introduce new general mechanics and some stages and area will be unlocked after you complete a particular stage. There are also 3 different characters to use although i doubt that there will be any difference except for their sfx when they are running. I have gotten used to the first female character which makes me can't focus when i switch it to the robot character. Each stage took less than 10 minutes to beat. However, you'll spend more time to beat it because you have to remember and practice for each patterns in every stage. In the last level of each area, the view will be slightly altered which can hurt your eyes (especially the last stage in the last area, Dark X Boson). When you died (and fail to complete the stage), there will be a graph which shows your progress in the last few runs. I really like the design because i can see how far i'm improved. I don't know the reason why, but you can't pause mid game. If you have to do an important stuff when you're aiming for high score, you're doomed. There is also no restart button in case you messed up. However, this won't really matter because you can kill yourself easily. Pros: - 18 stages - 3 different characters - Challenging stages - High scores Cons: - Some level hurts your eyes - Can't pause mid game - No restart button This is a fast paced runner game which focused on eye hand coordination. There are 18 different stages with 3 different playable characters. You can only win the stage either by skill or luck.

You can shoot through nearly every surface of the game allowing for some intresting ways of tackling levels.  Enemies will kill you in a single hit and there can be a lot of them so its a nice balance between tatical and reflex gaming. The most intresting mechanic is the Bros themselves.  You start off as a rambo clone with a machine gun, greanades, and one life but its not long before you find a POW and upon saving them you switch to a new unlocked Bro with different weapons and a different playstyle and you get an extra life.  Every time you save a POW or die you switch to a random Bro and every few POWs you save unlocks a new Bro.  This will constantly force you to change up your tactics and you'll want to keep playing to see the next movie parody Bro unlocked. Outside of Unlocking Bros There are an intresting variety of enemies and hazords and some really cool boss fights to keep you entertained as well as online drop in drop out co-op play.  The campain itself will last you 5-7 hours and it lets you play from the start with all you unlocked Bros which adds to the replay value. My only gripes are that the jumping is very floaty which lead to a lot of cheap deaths and that some Bros are way more useful then others.  You'll scream when your trying to past a wave of bullets and the game keeps giving you melee characters when all you want is a gun. Overall the game is simple and fun with lots of colorful characters and a very aware sense of humor.  Ideal to pick up and play for a couple of hours at a time.
